decision.explanation: The provided evidence (pmid-33035457:f01) describes a phase 2 trial of tazemetostat in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, a subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The study explicitly stratified patients by EZH2 status (mutant vs wild-type) and reported an objective response rate of 69% in the EZH2 mutant cohort compared to 35% in the wild-type cohort. This differential response rate directly supports the claim that somatic EZH2 activating mutations are associated with sensitivity/response to tazemetostat in this disease context. The claim is fully evidenced by the source data.

citations.quote: Activating mutations of EZH2, an epigenetic regulator, are present in approximately 20% of patients with follicular lymphoma. . . . Patients were categorised by EZH2 status: mutant (EZH2mut) or wild-type (EZH2WT). Patients received 800 mg of tazemetostat . . . The objective response rate was 69% (95% CI 53-82; 31 of 45 patients) in the EZH2mut cohort and 35% (23-49; 19 of 54 patients) in the EZH2WT cohort.
